findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: At least three shelves inside of the walk in cooler were observed with dried debris. The shelves are used to store food, while some food items were uncovered and could possibility be exposed to cross contamination. Discussed and shown to the PIC. Ensure that shelves are taken outdoors to be power washed and cleaned to remove the unwanted debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: There is a bit of ice build up on the floor underneath the shelves of the indoor walk in cooler (shelves mentioned in violation #49). Shown to the PIC. Ensure that the ice is removed and that the cooler is maintained free of ice accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There was grease buildup observed along the floor and the wall behind the cookline in the kitchen area. Shown to the PIC. Be sure that a cleaning schedule is in place to ensure that employees are frequently cleaning hard to reach areas (behind cookline) to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: There wasn’t any bleach available for responding to a vomit or diarrheal event. Discussed with PIC that bleach should be purchased in order to properly respond to a Norovirus event. The bleach must contain an EPA registration number. Ensure that bleach is purchased and available by the March 2, 2025 followup date.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink in the dish room lacked paper towels and also hand soap. Discussed with the person-in-charge that every handsink shall be stocked with the essentials for proper handwashing. Ensure that every handsink has warm running water, handsoap, and paper towels at all times. Will follow up on March 2, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a temperature measuring device available for the heat sanitizing dish machine. A temperature measuring device is necessary for ensuring that the machine is effectively sanitizing food contact surfaces. The person-in-charge mentioned that the facility will purchase thermo stickers in the near future. Ensure that a temperature measuring device is available to monitor sanitizing temperatures. Will follow-up on March 2, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.115 Warewashing Machines, Temperature Measuring Devices. A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; and (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Various surfaces of the fryer were observed heavily accumulated with grease and food debris. Shown to PIC. The surfaces included inside of the fryer, the outer surface of the fryer, and underneath and around the walls of the fryer. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is an unused steam table stored across from the serving line, as well as an unused cabinet that is stored inside of the dry storage room. Discussed with PIC that items that are no longer needed for operation shall be removed from the premises. Ensure that items are removed, as this may create a harboring environment for unwanted pest and insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
None of the employees, other than the only employee who holds a food manager certificate, could produce a copy of their food handler certificate. Discussed with the person-in-charge that all employees who handle clean dishes or food must obtain food handler certificates. Ensure that every employee has a food handler certificate on file by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A significant amount of mold buildup was observed on the bag of mozzarella cheese stored in the main kitchen’s 2 door cooler. Discussed and shown to PIC. The molded cheese was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that food is always safe for consumption and never containing mold or any other contaminant.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- There was loose food debris observed on the floor of the dry storage area (underneath racks storing dry goods).
- There was a significant amount of ice buildup (and food debris) on the floor of the indoor walk in freezer 
Ensure that these areas are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen area was tested at 0ppm (quat). The PIC stated that the facility created the bucket earlier in the morning. The sani bucket was recreated and tested again at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize food contact surfaces and utensils.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Various cheeses such as but not limited to sliced American and shredded cheddar were probed at 51F and 53F. The temperature knob of the cooler was observed at the number 5. The facility was instructed to adjust the temperature knob to a higher number to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. 1% milk was recorded again 43F. PIC stated that the cooler was recently serviced because of the unit freezing. Ensure that TCS foods are always maintained at 41F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The 2 door cooler in the serving area was observed with improper cold holding temperatures. The inside hanging thermometers read 50F and 51F. The temperature knob was observed at the number 5. The facility was instructed to adjust the knob to a higher number to lower the temperature of the unit. The ambient temperature of the unit was recorded again at 48F.  Ensure that cold holding units are sufficient enough to provide proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Accumulated soil and food debris were observed in the following areas:

1. The microwave was observed at to have an accumulation of grease drips and food debris on the base. 
2. Inspector observed the buildup of black mold in the far right compartment of the triple sink in the kitchen.
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that the above mention areas would be cleaned. Ensure that non food contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed there to be no hand soap at the handwashing sink in the dish room. Discussed with PIC and hand soap was provided. Ensure that soap is always available at each hand-sink to wash hands properly. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed an expired gallon of 2% milk in the 2 door standing cooler. The manufacturer’s use by date was 4/29/2024. The milk gallon was discarded by an employee. Ensure that milks never exceed the manufacturer’s use by date and are discarded if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for raw food storage and sanitization. Sanitizer was not available for use and not connected at the wall mounted dispenser above the 3 part sink. There was no clear indication as to how long sanitizer had been absent from the facility. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sign was not posted at the basin designated for handwashing at the kitchen 2 part sink. Handwashing sign was posted after the last inspection. A new handwashing sign was provided to be posted. Ensure handwashing signs are maintained at designated handwashing sinks.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Carton of raw shell eggs was observed on a shelf above ready to eat foods in the sliding door cooler up front. Eggs were relocated to the bottom of the cooler. PIC noted eggs are intended for residential units and was unsure as to why the product was in the cooler. Ensure raw eggs are stored on the bottom shelf below and separate from ready to eat foods if/when stored in this cooler. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer was not present at the wall mounted dispenser above the kitchen 3 part sink. Employee in the kitchen noted they were using soap solution to wipe down everything, and there was no clear indication as to how long quat sanitizer was absent. Quat product was not available and needs to be ordered. PIC stated they would contact their supplier today to order more product. Bleach is available for use. A solution at 200ppm was prepared in the sani-bucket during inspection. Bleach solutions will be used until quat product is once again available. Quat test strips were ordered since the last inspection, and chlorine test strips were given to PIC by inspector. A ready to use cleaner/sanitizer with active ingredients of DDBSA/lactic acid was present but cannot be used in the kitchen until test strips are available (see General Comments for additional information). Inspector will follow-up on availability of quat sanitizer at follow-up in 10 days (9/28/23).
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for wiping surfaces. Bleach solution was provided during inspection.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing and glove use. The designated PIC does not currently have a manager certification but is working to complete certification. PIC was unfamiliar with employee health policy requirements as well as other aspects of facility operations. The need to demonstrate knowledge and perform duties as designated PIC were discussed. PIC is new to the facility and still in the process of learning processes and procedures since starting in late 2022. PIC felt they had a better understanding of several topics by the conclusion of the inspection. Completing the food manager course will provide additional knowledge to aid in effective management of the facility. Active managerial controls will be revisited at the next routine inspection after PIC has the opportunity to complete manager course. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Designated PIC does not currently have a food manager certification. One of the employees working at the time of inspection has a manager certification, but the PIC is required to be a certified food protection manager. PIC noted they are registered to take a food manager course next week.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents were not available at the time of inspection. PIC was not familiar with the requirement and noted the reporting agreement did not look familiar. Employee health documents were provided and discussed with emphasis on knowledge required by management and staff on reporting illness and time frame for exclusion from food handling depending on reportable symptoms versus being diagnosed with and/or potentially exposed to foodborne pathogens. All staff signed reporting agreements at the time of inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique at the right basin of the two part sink. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and educational handout was provided.
 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Facility has one handwashing sink in the dish area. When asked about potential use of one basin at the two part sink, PIC and staff indicated they only use the handwashing sink in the dish area. An employee was later observed washing hands at the right basin of the two part sink. A paper towel dispenser was located on the wall to the right, and a pump bottle of soap was retrieved from the shelf above the sink when hands were washed. Moving forward, the right basin of the two part sink will be designated for handwashing only and will be supplied with handwashing signage in addition to soap and paper towels. **See General Comments for additional information**
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 (A) Employees were observed misusing single use gloves. One employee touched a garbage can with gloved hands and did not change gloves prior to conducting temperature checks. Employees were observed entering and exiting the kitchen through a closed door with gloved hands to access walk-in cooler and storage area. Also while wearing gloves, one employee was observed scratching their face, and employees were observed adjusting clothing. Proper glove use was discussed with all staff, and effort was made to change gloves more frequently as needed between tasks. Educational handout on proper glove use was provided. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for wiping surfaces. New solution was provided during inspection. Maintain sanitizer solution during all hours of operation.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Facility is not in compliance with food handler law. One employee had a food handler certification that expired as of December 2022. Ensure re-certification occurs before the next routine inspection, and be mindful to renew certifications prior to expiration.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
There were no paper towels observed at the hand sink near the dish machine. Paper towels were stocked during the inspection. Ensure all hand sinks are stocked with soap and paper towels. 
 
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed shelves in the walk in cooler to have mold and other accumulation on them. Ensure shelves and other non-food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently so they are maintained clean.  
\
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to reach a temperature of 151F during the inspection. The dish machine must be at least 160F in order to properly sanitize dishes. 
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.
